He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Champagnie was born in New York, New York and grew up in [[Brooklyn]]. He attended [[Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School]]. As a senior, he averaged 19.8 points per game and was named first team Class AA All-State. A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] over offers from [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]], [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] and [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].{{cite web|url=https://triblive.com/sports/pitt-signs-four-star-wing-player-to-letter-of-intent/|title=Pitt signs 4-star wing player to letter of intent|work=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]|date=April 18, 2019}} ==College career== As a true freshman, Champagnie led the Panthers with 12.7 points and 7 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2020/05/15/pitt-panthers-basketball-justin-champagnie-jeff-capel-exit-interview/stories/202005150046|title=2020 Pitt basketball exit interview: Justin Champagnie|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=March 15, 2020|access-date=December 25, 2020}} He was named the CBS Sports/USBWA National Freshman of the Week and the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Freshman of the Week after averaging 25 points and 10 rebounds in games against [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] and [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/freshman-rankings-pitts-justin-champagnie-is-freshman-of-the-week-teams-slumping-with-frosh-watch-stars/|title=Freshman rankings: Pitt's Justin Champagnie is Freshman of the Week; teams slumping with Frosh Watch stars|first=Matt|last=Norlander|website=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=February 11, 2020|access-date=December 25, 2020}}{{cite web |last=Meyer |first=Craig |date=February 12, 2020 |title=Justin Champagnie blossoming into Pitt's latest freshman star |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2020/02/12/pitt-panthers-basketball-justin-champagnie-xavier-johnson-trey-mcgowens-jeff-capel-acc/stories/202002110121 |access-date=December 25, 2020 |work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}} On December 22, 2020, Champagnie was ruled out for at least six weeks after sustaining a knee injury during practice.{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=December 22, 2020 |title=Pittsburgh Panthers leading scorer Justin Champagnie out 6-8 weeks |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30584701 |access-date=December 25, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} On January 19, 2021, he recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds in a 79–73 win over [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]].{{cite web |last=Rego |first=Max |title=Champagnie Showers: Pittsburgh upsets Duke men's basketball behind Justin Champagnie's dominance |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2021/01/duke-basketball-pittsburgh-justin-champagnie-jalen-johnson-matthew-hurt-acc-player-of-the-year |website=[[Duke Chronicle]] |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=January 19, 2021}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Champagnie was selected to the First Team All-ACC. As a sophomore, Champagnie averaged 18 points, 11.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.3 blocks per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last=DiPaola |first=Jerry |title=Justin Champagnie decides to leave Pitt, declare for the NBA Draft |url=https://triblive.com/sports/justin-champagnie-decides-to-leave-pitt-declare-for-the-nba-draft/ |access-date=July 2, 2021 |work=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]] |date=May 10, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors / Raptors 905 (2021–2022)=== Champagnie was projected as a late first-round pick to an early second-round pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. After going undrafted during the 2021 NBA draft, Champagnie signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on August 7, 2021, splitting time with their [[G League]] affiliate, [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web |last=Lopez |first=J. |date=August 7, 2021 |title=Raptors Sign Wainright & Champagnie |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-wainright-champagnie |access-date=August 7, 2021 |work=NBA.com}} With [[Scottie Barnes]] injured and unable to play,{{cite news |title=Raptors rookie Scottie Barnes out for Monday's game against Knicks |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-rookie-scottie-barnes-mondays-game-knicks/ |access-date=November 4, 2021 |work=Sportsnet.ca |date=November 1, 2021 |language=en}} Champagnie was called by the Raptors to make his professional debut on November 1, 2021, scoring his first two points in the NBA on free throws in a win against the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite news |last=Michalowski |first=George |title=Justin Champagnie Scores First NBA Points in Raptors' Win Over Knicks |url=https://pittsburghsportsnow.com/2021/11/02/justin-champagnie-makes-nba-debut-in-raptors-win-over-knicks/ |access-date=November 4, 2021 |work=Pittsburgh Sports Now |date=November 2, 2021}} Champagnie during his time in Toronto was mentored by All-NBA forward [[Pascal Siakam]] and became close with Champagnie seeing Siakam as a big brother.{{Cite web |last=Quinn |first=Justin |date=April 7, 2023 |title=Justin Champagnie on joining the Boston Celtics, facing the Toronto Raptors |url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2023/04/07/nba-boston-celtics-jc-vs-tor/ |access-date=October 25, 2024 |website=Celtics Wire |language=en-US}} On July 14, 2022, Champagnie re-signed with the Raptors on a two-year contract.{{Cite web |last=Beloso |first=M. |date=July 14, 2022 |title=RAPTORS SIGN CHAMPAGNIE |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-champagnie |access-date=July 14, 2022 }} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2023)=== On January 10, 2023, Champagnie was claimed off waivers by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Skyforce acquires Justin Champagnie|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-justin-champagnie|website=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2023|access-date=January 12, 2023}} ===Boston Celtics (2023)=== On April 7, 2023, Champagnie signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Forward Justin Champagnie|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/celtics-sign-forward-justin-champagnie|website=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} He appeared in two games for Boston, recording averages of 2.5 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. On July 31, Champagnie was waived by the Celtics.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Celtics Waive Justin Champagnie|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/08/celtics-waive-justin-champagnie.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 1, 2023|access-date=August 6, 2023}} ===Return to Sioux Falls (2023–2024)=== On August 11, 2023, Champagnie signed with the [[Miami Heat]],{{cite web|title=HEAT MAKE ROSTER MOVES|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-make-roster-moves|website=NBA.com|date=August 11, 2023|access-date=August 12, 2023}} but was waived on October 21, prior to the start of the 2023–24 season.{{cite web|title=HEAT WAIVE CHAMPAGNIE AND DIALLO|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-champagnie-and-diallo|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2023}} Nine days later, he returned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2023-24 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=January 28, 2024}} ===Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2024–present)=== On February 22, 2024, Champagnie signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]]{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Justin Champagnie to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-justin-champagnie-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2024|access-date=February 22, 2024}} and on March 3, he signed a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Champagnie to Two-Way Contract/Sign Hampton to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-champagnie-to-two-way-contract-sign-hampton-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 3, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2024}} On February 10, 2025, Justin played against his twin brother [[Julian Champagnie|Julian]] for the first time in an NBA game, when the Wizards met the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|title=Oh, brother: As Champagnie twins have a moment, Spurs turn back Wizards|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2025/02/10/wizards-spurs-champagnie-twins/|website=washingtonpost.com|last=Shankar|first=Varun|date=February 11, 2025|access-date=February 11, 2025}} They are among a very small number of twins who have ever played against one another in an NBA game.{{Cite web|title=How many sets of twins have played in the NBA?|url=https://fansided.com/2023/06/22/how-many-sets-twins-nba-history//|website=fansided.com|date=June 22, 2023|last=Wilson|first=Josh|access-date=February 11, 2025}} On March 2, Champagnie and the Wizards agreed to a four-year, $10 million contract.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=March 2, 2025 |title=Wizards, Justin Champagnie finalizing 4-year deal, web|url=https://iriefm.net/washington-wizards-sign-justin-champagnie-to-four-year-deal-amid-fiba-americas-pre-qualifiers-interest-from-jamaica/|title=Washington Wizards sign Justin Champagnie to professional basketball for the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2020/02/05/justin-and-julian-champagnie-find-success-apart-for-first-time/|title=Justin and Julian Champagnie they later became teammates on the Wizards in 2026.{{Cite web|title=Inside how ascending agent Daniel Hazan got four clients signed by the Wizards|url=https://www.bulletsforever.com/washington-wizards-miscellaneous/68392/inside-how-ascending-agent-daniel-hazan-got-four-clients-signed-by-the-wizards|access-date=June 8, 2026|website=bulletsforever.com|language=en}} Champagnie is a multi-generational New Yorker, raised in [[Kensington, Brooklyn]]. His mother's family is from [[Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn]], and his father grew up in the Bronx after immigrating from [[Jamaica]].{{Cite news |last=Orsborn |first=Tom |title=Spurs' 'Brooklyn baby'
